verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'lifted off from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R2: 'April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC (6:35:12 p.m. EDT) ... Launch site Kennedy, LC-39B'; R3: 'launched on 1 April 2026 at 6.35pm Eastern Time'; R5: 'launched ... on April 1 ... at 6:35 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly confirm the exact date, time, and location of the successful launch.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The first crewed deep-space flight in over 50 years'; R2: 'the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972'; R5: 'first humans back to the Moon in over 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: References explicitly state it is the first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972, over 50 years prior.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission sent four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the Moon and back to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II mission around the Moon'; R2: 'Crew size 4 ... approximately ten-day trip'; R3: 'four-person crew ... 10-day mission ... looped around the Moon'; R4: 'four-person crew ... 10-day mission'; R5: 'crew of four astronauts ... 10-day mission around the Moon and back'
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm four astronauts on a roughly 10-day lunar flyby mission.

verifications.claim: The mission goal of the Artemis II mission is a 10-day crewed lunar flyby test mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA’s Artemis II test flight ... approximately 10-day Artemis II mission around the Moon'; R2: 'Artemis II (April 1–11, 2026) was a crewed lunar flyby mission ... test flight'; R3: '10-day mission, the four-person crew circled around Earth ... looped around the Moon'; R5: '10-day mission around the Moon and back ... test flight'
verifications.reasoning: References describe it as a test mission involving a crewed 10-day lunar flyby.

verifications.claim: The launch vehicle for the Artemis II mission is the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA’s Artemis II SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'; R2: 'Rocket Space Launch System'; R3: 'Space Launch System (SLS)'; R4: 'Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'; R5: 'Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'
verifications.reasoning: All references explicitly identify SLS as the launch vehicle.

verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Nasa plans another crewed test mission, Artemis III, in 2027'
verifications.reasoning: Only R4 mentions 2027 for Artemis III; others omit specific dates or focus on changes/delays without confirming 2027.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is a crew landing mission.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R3: 'changed Artemis 3 to another demonstration mission, with a human moon landing ... during Artemis 4'; R4: 'another crewed test mission, Artemis III ... to rehearse Orion's rendezvous and docking'; R5: 'Artemis III, a crewed test where Orion will dock with a lunar lander ... Artemis IV ... first crewed Moon landing'
verifications.reasoning: References explicitly state Artemis III is a test/demo/rendezvous mission, not a landing; landing shifted to Artemis IV.

verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'lunar landing ... Artemis IV mission, planned for 2028 ... another landing later in 2028 with the Artemis V mission'; R5: 'Artemis IV ... by 2028'
verifications.reasoning: References mention some subsequent missions (Artemis IV/V) targeted for 2028, but phrasing is approximate and not all subsequent missions specified for exactly 2028.
